messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Mercy General private deployment constraints & next steps

Hi Rajiv / Anita —

Thanks again for the 60-minute walkthrough today. Quick recap of what I heard and the immediate asks so we can keep momentum: 

Top pain points / constraints
- PHI and regulated patient data must remain on-prem (no long-term egress permitted).
- Security team requires SOC2 Type II evidence and FIPS-compatible HSM/KMS integration for key material.
- Network is tightly restricted: outbound only via company NAT/proxy, no direct internet from compute hosts, and strict IP whitelisting.
- Procurement prefers a single-vendor SOW for the private deployment with clear rollback/fallback plan.

Goals we discussed
1) Validate that Redwood Private can be deployed inside Mercy's VPC/on-prem with no persistent outbound egress other than control-plane TLS to allow updates or, alternately, a fully air-gapped install.
2) Agree on a technical deep-dive (SRE <> Redwood infra) to map out IP ranges, ports, and bootstrap options.
3) Produce an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) + high-level estimate for Dedicated/Private sizing and OPEX.

Clarifications / notes from the call
- We will support HSM integration (PKCS#11) but need details on your vendor/version to confirm driver support.
- For air-gapped installs: we provide an offline bundle + install checklist; net-new customers typically run a pre-provisioned appliance image and then we sync artifacts via USB/air-gap transfer.
- For VPC-based Private: minimal outbound is port 443 to our control plane for license checks/metrics by default; we can discuss a fully isolated mode for procurement.

Attachments I’m sending with this email:
- redwood_onprem_prereqs.pdf — high-level pre-reqs and port/IP checklist (initial).

Next steps (proposed)
1) Schedule a 90-min technical deep-dive w/ your SRE and network team (please propose times).
2) Mercy to send a sanitized network diagram and confirm HSM vendor + SSO provider.
3) Redwood to send a draft MAP and an offline-install checklist within 24 hours.

I’ll follow up with Dev and Vivek internally to prepare the technical checklist tailored to your topology.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Tessa —

Thanks for the crisp summary, that aligns with what we need. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) When you say "minimal outbound on 443 for control plane" — can you provide the specific FQDNs and IP ranges we need to whitelist? Our security policy requires CIDR-level rules or cert pins before anything is allowed.
2) For HSM: we currently have a Thales Luna SA cluster (FIPS 140-2). Will Redwood’s PKCS#11 integration work with Luna out of the box, or is there an adapter/consulting engagement required?
3) For the air-gapped option, can you confirm the maximum artifact size for the offline bundle and whether we need to bring any USBs to the install window?
4) Timeline: our procurement window is tight — we are targeting a pilot by end of Q1 2027. Need an early ballpark on cost/timelines to route internally.

Subject: RE: Mercy General - technical checklist (prepping for deep-dive)

Folks —

I pulled together an internal checklist based on the call and Rajiv’s topology. Posting the high-level items we should confirm during the SRE deep-dive: 

Network & bootstrap
- Exact outbound FQDNs for control plane: control.redwood.ai, updates.redwood.ai. We can provide /32s but prefer FQDN whitelisting behind proxy.
- IP/port needs: 443 outbound for control plane; 443 for image artifact retrieval (if not air-gapped). No persistent inbound ports required.
- For SSH access during install: optional jump-host (port 22) via customer-managed bastion — we support both.
- Proxy auth: support for proxy with basic auth and mTLS; need sample proxy config if Mercy uses TLS interception.

Security & keys
- HSM: PKCS#11 compatible — we’ve validated with Thales Luna in v7.x in prior deployments but need exact firmware and API exposure.
- KMS: support for BYOK with key-material import; recommend we map key rotation cadence in MAP.

Air-gap / offline install
- Offline bundle size: typically ~3.2GB for the runtime artifacts and ~500MB for model shards (varies by model). We can produce a trimmed bundle for pilot.
- Media: USB 3.0 or transport via secured internal transfer; installation window typically 2–4 hours for baseline infra + smoke tests.

Compliance artifacts
- We’ll pull together our SOC2 summary and runbook excerpts; security can also supply a high-level design doc for their review.

Action items for the deep-dive call
1) Get exact HSM model/firmware and SSO provider (for SCIM/SAML integrations).
2) Get sanitized network CIDRs and proxy config (we can accept FQDNs but procurement may want /32 ranges).
3) Confirm whether the pilot requires air-gap or if a controlled outbound path is acceptable.

I’ll draft the technical appendix to the MAP and attach a trimmed offline bundle example for the call. Tessa — I recommend we schedule the deep-dive next Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Dev

- Offline bundle: we can produce a trimmed pilot bundle ~2.8GB (models and runtime trimmed to your pilot scope). We recommend providing a USB-3 encrypted thumb or secure transfer to the datacenter. Our onsite install window estimate: 3 hours for infra + 1–2 hours for smoke tests with your SRE.
